## Setup and Libraries
```{r setup}
#| message: no
#| warning: no

library(spatstat)
library(imager)
library(anndataR)
library(parallel)
library(spatstat)
library(rhdf5)
```


I'm going to read all the sample adatas and the masks and add them togheter to create point process objects, then I'll reduce the dimensionality of the pp objects so I can estimate the Lcross function between two cell types of interest, by now they are Neoplastic and Stromal cells.

## Path Configuration

Dynamically configure paths for input, output, and masks based on document parameters.
```{r paths-handling}
# Directories
sample_dir <-  "/projects/shared/TCGA_data/h5ad/TCGA-TS-A7P8-01Z-00-DX1.25E9AFA9-6C12-4F18-BE79-2F4F19887ECD.h5ad.gz"
save_dir <-  "/projects/shared/TCGA_data/results/test"

# Generate the save path
file_name <- sub("\\.h5ad\\.gz$", ".rds", basename(sample_dir))
save_path <- file.path(save_dir, file_name)

# Configure path for the mask (.png)
mask_path <- sub("/h5ad/", "/mask/", sample_dir)
mask_path <- sub("\\.h5ad\\.gz$", ".png", mask_path)
```


## Data Loading and PPP Conversion

Load the mask image and convert the spatial annotation file into a Point Pattern (`ppp`) object compatible with `spatstat`.

The function need the h5ad file path, the mask as an image and combine them together based on magnification level, 
it's needed to specify the column of the h5ad with the cell type information, and the name of the spatial coordinate, by default named "x" and "y". 

Read the mask as an image
```{r mask-import}
img <- imager::load.image(mask_path)
```


Create the point process object
```{r}
AppMag <-  40

pp_object <- ann2ppp(sample_dir, mask = img, magnif = AppMag)
```


## Downsampling (KDE)

To prevent memory overflow, we apply a Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) based downsampling before computing the `Lcross` function between Neoplastic and Stromal cells.

Function to downsample based on the Kernel Density Estimation, it needs a pp objects, the marks name which is a vector of dim 2 and a target number of point to which downsample. It's possible to personalized the density.ppp function

Creation of the subsetted pp object
```{r pp-subsetting}
# Define the distance vector
r_values <- seq(0, 150, length.out = 70)

# Reproducibility for downsampling
set.seed(10)
ppp_sub <- downsample_KDE(pp_object, c("neoplastic", "stromal"), 40000)
```


Estimating the Lcross function between the two cell types with the subsetted pp object
```{r}
# Compute Lcross function
Lcross_neoStroma <- Lcross(
  ppp_sub, 
  i = "neoplastic", 
  j = "stromal", 
  r = r_values,
  correction = "border"
)
```


## Saving Results

Export the resulting analysis object into a serialized `.rds` format.
```{r save-output}
#| eval: no

saveRDS(Lcross_neoStroma, file = save_path)
```
